mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% (FEDFUNDS) consistently predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns due to accommodative monetary policy supporting equity valuations.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 0.5% occurs in more than 20% of 20-day windows, but the positive return rate is below 55% (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 270, it signals high inflation that leads to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to expected monetary tightening and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 270 occurs in more than 20% of 20-day windows, but the negative return rate is below 55% (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0% AND the employment level (PAYEMS) declines month-over-month, it signals a deteriorating labor market that leads to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The condition (UNRATE > 5.0% AND PAYEMS change < 0) occurs in more than 20% of 20-day windows, but the negative return rate is below 55% (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%), a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and month-over-month change > 0.01%) signals monetary tightening that leads to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% AND FEDFUNDS > 2.0% AND FEDFUNDS change > 0.01%
failure_condition: The condition (UNRATE < 4.0% AND FEDFUNDS > 2.0% AND FEDFUNDS change > 0.01%) occurs in more than 20% of 20-day windows, but the negative return rate is below 55% (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1600 (thousands of units), it predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns due to strong economic activity and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1600 occurs in more than 20% of 20-day windows, but the positive return rate is below 55% (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 100 (index value), it signals strong economic activity that leads to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 100 occurs in more than 20% of 20-day windows, but the positive return rate is below 55% (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) exceed 600,000 million dollars AND housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1500 (thousands of units), it signals strong consumer and housing demand that leads to positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The condition (RSAFS > 600000 AND HOUST > 1500) occurs in more than 20% of 5-day windows, but the positive return rate is below 55% (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a strong demand regime (RSAFS > 600,000 AND HOUST > 1500), a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and month-over-month change > 0.01%) predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 returns due to expected monetary tightening.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 600000 AND HOUST > 1500 AND FEDFUNDS > 2.0% AND FEDFUNDS change > 0.01%
failure_condition: The condition (RSAFS > 600000 AND HOUST > 1500 AND FEDFUNDS > 2.0% AND FEDFUNDS change > 0.01%) occurs in more than 20% of 60-day windows, but the negative return rate is below 55% (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.
